You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

To list the historical battles in the database:

```sql
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  date,
  bulgarian_commander,
  latin_commander,
  result
FROM battle;
```
only want battles where more than 10 people died

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  SUM(d.killed) AS total_killed
FROM battle AS b
JOIN ship AS s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death AS d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result
HAVING SUM(d.killed) > 10;
```
make sure the total deaths across all involved adds up to over 10

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_deaths
FROM battle AS b
LEFT JOIN ship AS s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death AS d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.bulgarian_commander,
  b.latin_commander,
  b.result
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) > 10;
```
add battle names with their IDs too

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_deaths
FROM battle AS b
LEFT JOIN ship AS s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death AS d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id,
  b.name
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) > 10;
```
Also need to include unique identifiers for the battles.

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS unique_battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_deaths
FROM battle AS b
LEFT JOIN ship AS s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death AS d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY
  b.id,
  b.name
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) > 10;
```
